result.title: Aircraft transit report module

facts.text: Scope is a backend feature module at `apps/backend/src/modules/aircraft-transits/` plus its database table. No HTTP controller, no worker consumer.
facts.comment: endpoint to get available airports and aircraft. store in DB using seed

facts.text: Reports are synthetic: any two airports, a Turf great-circle path, and a mock aircraft. OpenSky is not used.
Input is origin ICAO code, destination ICAO code, and departure time. Codes are compared case-insensitively.
Airport name, country, and lat/lon come from the NOAA aviationweather.gov airport API behind an `AirportDirectory` port. The base URL comes from an env variable.
If NOAA returns no airport for a code, the result is an `UnknownAirportError` naming that code.
If NOAA is unreachable, times out, or returns a non-2xx status, the result is an `AirportDirectoryUnavailableError`, marked as transient so the worker can retry later.
If origin equals destination, the result is a `SameAirportError`, returned before any NOAA call.
`ValidateAircraftTransitRequestUseCase` checks unknown airports, same airport, and departure in the past (`DepartureInPastError`). It returns the resolved airports and saves nothing.
`GenerateAircraftTransitReportUseCase` runs the same private validator except the past-departure check, so queued or retried jobs don't fail because time moved on.
The distance is the great-circle distance in km, computed with Turf.
The mock aircraft is picked from a static list of real models, each with a cruise speed. It gets a random registration.
Arrival time = departure time + distance / cruise speed. The report includes departure, arrival, and duration in minutes.
The path has one waypoint per ~100 km (at least 2), follows the great circle, and starts and ends exactly at the airport coordinates.
Each waypoint has lat, lon, timestamp, altitude (m), and speed (km/h). Timestamps increase from departure to arrival.
Altitude is 0 at both airports and cruise altitude in the middle, with a linear climb over the first 10% and descent over the last 10% of the distance.
A route crossing the antimeridian (e.g. RJTT → KSFO) still produces one continuous, valid waypoint list.
The report exposes the path as a GeoJSON LineString built from the waypoints in [lon, lat] order. It is not stored separately.
Generation simulates work with a random 1–3 s delay behind a replaceable seam. Tests use zero delay and fakes, with no real network calls.
Reports are saved in the `aircraft_transit_reports` table with id `atr_<ULID>`: scalar columns for airports, times, distance, and aircraft, plus a jsonb `waypoints` column. A migration is included.
`GetAircraftTransitReportUseCase` returns a saved report by id, or an `AircraftTransitReportNotFoundError`.
Use cases return neverthrow `Result`s, with error classes owned by the feature. They contain no HTTP or retry decisions.
`DECISIONS.md`, `apps/backend/AGENTS.md`, and `.env.example` document the module, the NOAA source, the validation split, and the new env variable.
`pnpm check` passes.

result.factsMarkdown:
# Facts

- Reports are synthetic: any two airports, a Turf great-circle path, and a mock aircraft. OpenSky is not used.
- Input is origin ICAO code, destination ICAO code, and departure time. Codes are compared case-insensitively.
- Airport name, country, and lat/lon come from the NOAA aviationweather.gov airport API behind an `AirportDirectory` port. The base URL comes from an env variable.
- If NOAA returns no airport for a code, the result is an `UnknownAirportError` naming that code.
- If NOAA is unreachable, times out, or returns a non-2xx status, the result is an `AirportDirectoryUnavailableError`, marked as transient so the worker can retry later.
- If origin equals destination, the result is a `SameAirportError`, returned before any NOAA call.
- `ValidateAircraftTransitRequestUseCase` checks unknown airports, same airport, and departure in the past (`DepartureInPastError`). It returns the resolved airports and saves nothing.
- `GenerateAircraftTransitReportUseCase` runs the same private validator except the past-departure check, so queued or retried jobs don't fail because time moved on.
- The distance is the great-circle distance in km, computed with Turf.
- The mock aircraft is picked from a static list of real models, each with a cruise speed. It gets a random registration.
- Arrival time = departure time + distance / cruise speed. The report includes departure, arrival, and duration in minutes.
- The path has one waypoint per ~100 km (at least 2), follows the great circle, and starts and ends exactly at the airport coordinates.
- Each waypoint has lat, lon, timestamp, altitude (m), and speed (km/h). Timestamps increase from departure to arrival.
- Altitude is 0 at both airports and cruise altitude in the middle, with a linear climb over the first 10% and descent over the last 10% of the distance.
- A route crossing the antimeridian (e.g. RJTT → KSFO) still produces one continuous, valid waypoint list.
- The report exposes the path as a GeoJSON LineString built from the waypoints in [lon, lat] order. It is not stored separately.
- Generation simulates work with a random 1–3 s delay behind a replaceable seam. Tests use zero delay and fakes, with no real network calls.
- Reports are saved in the `aircraft_transit_reports` table with id `atr_<ULID>`: scalar columns for airports, times, distance, and aircraft, plus a jsonb `waypoints` column. A migration is included.
- `GetAircraftTransitReportUseCase` returns a saved report by id, or an `AircraftTransitReportNotFoundError`.
- Use cases return neverthrow `Result`s, with error classes owned by the feature. They contain no HTTP or retry decisions.
- `DECISIONS.md`, `apps/backend/AGENTS.md`, and `.env.example` document the module, the NOAA source, the validation split, and the new env variable.
- `pnpm check` passes.
